security_audit.summary: All 16 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown references, schema fields, SQL identifiers, and ordinary safety guidance. One medium-risk semantic issue remains because an example report includes raw observed values and can print them to pipeline logs.

remediation.issue: Example validation reports can expose raw observed values in logs.
remediation.suggestion: Redact, hash, or aggregate observed values before storing report details or printing failed checks.

content.value_statement: Unreliable data pipelines create incorrect reports, failed models, and costly investigations. This skill designs practical checks, contracts, alerts, and validation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Defines checks for completeness, uniqueness, validity, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness.
Designs Great Expectations suites and checkpoints for schema, range, freshness, and statistical validation.
Creates dbt schema tests, generic tests, singular tests, and relationship checks.
Drafts data contracts with ownership, schemas, quality rules, privacy labels, and service levels.
Plans automated validation pipelines with reporting, alerts, ownership, and failure handling.
Provides implementation checklists, examples, and rollout guidance for critical datasets.
limitations: Examples require adaptation for installed framework versions, warehouse dialects, and project conventions.
The skill does not access data sources or execute validations without suitable tools and permissions.
Business rules, thresholds, and service levels require input from dataset owners.
Validation output can expose sensitive values unless reports and logs apply redaction.

use_cases.title: Protect Analytics Pipelines
use_cases.description: Add focused dbt tests for keys, accepted values, relationships, freshness, and row counts.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform Validation
use_cases.description: Create reusable Great Expectations suites, checkpoints, alerts, and failure policies across warehouse datasets.

use_cases.title: Define Producer Contracts
use_cases.description: Document schemas, ownership, privacy classifications, quality rules, and service levels for shared data products.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Quality Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a data quality plan for [dataset]. Include completeness, uniqueness, validity, and freshness checks for these columns: [columns].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a focused checklist for one dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Design a dbt Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Design dbt tests for [model] using this schema: [schema]. Include key, relationship, range, accepted-value, freshness, and row-count tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate a known model schema into layered dbt tests.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Validation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Great Expectations workflow for [datasets]. Define suites, checkpoints, schedules, alerts, owners, redaction rules, and nonblocking fallback behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan repeatable validation for several production datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Establish a Data Contract Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a versioned contract and rollout plan for [data product]. Cover schema compatibility, privacy, quality metrics, service levels, CI gates, and migration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate advanced governance across producers, consumers, and platform teams.

output_examples.input: Create quality checks for an orders model with order, customer, amount, status, and creation fields.
output: Order identifiers must be present and unique.
Customer identifiers must be present and match the customer model.
Amounts must be positive and remain within an approved business range.
Statuses must use the approved lifecycle values.
Creation timestamps must be valid, recent, and not in the future.

output_examples.input: Outline a production rollout for daily warehouse validation.
output: Start with warning-only checks on critical datasets.
Measure failure rates and adjust thresholds with dataset owners.
Route alerts to named owners with clear remediation steps.
Block pipelines only for stable critical checks with fallback procedures.
Review quality metrics and contract changes on a scheduled basis.

output_examples.input: Draft the scope for an orders data contract.
output: Identify the producer, consumers, owner, and support contact.
Define field types, required values, keys, privacy classifications, and compatibility rules.
Set freshness, availability, and latency objectives.
Document quality checks, change notices, and migration responsibilities.

best_practices: Prioritize critical datasets and columns before expanding validation coverage.
Version contracts and review thresholds with producers, consumers, and dataset owners.
Redact sensitive values from validation results, alerts, reports, and pipeline logs.
anti_patterns: Do not block production pipelines with uncalibrated checks or missing fallback procedures.
Do not hardcode thresholds without measuring normal behavior and documenting ownership.
Do not expose raw sensitive records when reporting failed validations.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Great Expectations, dbt tests, data contracts, and SodaCL quality specifications.

faq.question: Can it generate checks for an existing schema?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the schema, business rules, critical columns, and expected freshness.

faq.question: Does it run validation against my warehouse?
faq.answer: No. Execution requires configured tools, credentials, network access, and explicit permission.

faq.question: How should failed checks affect pipelines?
faq.answer: Begin with warnings, calibrate thresholds, and block only stable critical checks with documented fallback procedures.

faq.question: Can it help define data contracts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure ownership, schemas, privacy labels, quality rules, service levels, and change management.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Redact or aggregate observed values before storing results, sending alerts, or printing pipeline reports.
